description: JSON-driven queries for Entity Framework Core. A powerful, versatile library for dynamically composing complex filter, sort, paginate, group, aggregate, and set-operation (Union / Intersect / Except) expressions — all driven by simple JSON objects from any front-end or API consumer. Three composable shapes (Filter / Segment / Summary), twenty-eight extension methods, nested navigation through references and collections with auto-wrapped .Any() lambdas, heterogeneous Condition.Values with type-safe coercion, and a thread-safe reflection cache with five tuned presets (FIFO / LRU / LFU). Since 3.0 it also carries an opt-in field-level policy layer: attributes and runtime rules decide what each caller may filter, sort, select, group, aggregate and see, with masking, tokenization, forced predicates and a k-anonymity floor. Targets .NET 6+. Free Forever. Full reference, JSON cookbook, and tuning guide at https://doc.dynamicwhere.com.
releaseNotes:
v3.4.0 — Page caps per declared purpose, so an export reads every match in one statement while a search keeps its page; security fixes for struct members, a transform on one now applied, a member of a nullable struct now policed and a typed selection beneath a list of structs no longer handing back a denied member; a path through a member a constructor builds is refused rather than run; the parts of a struct take the struct member's policy; and a typed selection through a struct returns its values.

Security fix: a transform declared on a member of an application's own struct was never applied. [DwMask], [DwGeneralize], [DwFormat], [DwTruncate], [DwDefault] and [DwMutate], Hash and Tokenize included, on a struct's member left the stored value in the result, in both tiers, from rows in memory and from EF Core, whenever the struct was carried by a whole row or selected whole, typed or dynamic. The outbound walk read the struct as a copy in a box, and the setter unboxed a second copy to write into, so each transform landed on a temporary. Present in every release since 3.0.0; a class member was never affected. The setter now writes into the box in place, and both passes of the walk write each changed struct back where it was read from, innermost first: into its member, into its position in a list or an array, or into the struct holding it. A member the policy names is transformed once. Behaviour change (fail-closed): a struct a transform changed that cannot be written back, held by a member with no setter, in a collection that cannot be written by position such as a HashSet, or as a dictionary's value, now fails the query with InvalidOperationException rather than emitting the stored value.

Security fix: a member of a nullable struct was not policed. A query reaches a member of an Iban? through the nullable, Iban.Value.Number, while the attribute walk, the transforms and the fragments name the member Iban.Number, so a lookup by the query's spelling matched none of them: a [DwDenied] on the nullable member or on a member of the struct did not stop a filter, a sort, a grouping key or a selection of that member, Iban.HasValue was open, and a mask on a member of the struct was not applied when a selection named it through Value, as a result column or as a group key. Present in every release since 3.0.0; the typed selection fix below had widened it to the typed terminal before release. A Value after a nullable struct of the application's is now dropped wherever the policy reads a path: the resolver, the outbound walk, the summary's key and aggregate transforms, the group floor and the past-depth transforms. A nullable's own members, HasValue included, are read as the nullable member, and the walk reaches a member a dynamic projection's generated row holds under Value.

Security fix: a typed selection naming a path beneath a collection of an application's own structs handed back each element whole. Selects ["Pairs.Shown"] over a List of Pair structs returned every Pair with all its members, a [DwDenied] one included, in both tiers, while the policy had approved Pairs.Shown alone; the typed projection bound every collection of values whole, which is right for strings, numbers and dates and wrong for a struct. Present in every release since 3.0.0; the dynamic terminal was never affected. Each element is now built member by member into a list or an array, a null collection stays null, and a collection of nullable structs or of another shape is left unbound rather than carried whole. Selecting the collection whole is refused when an element's member is denied, as it was. Behaviour change: a typed selection beneath a list of structs that an EF Core projection builds with a collection initializer, Pairs = new List<Pair> { new Pair { ... } }, now fails in EF Core's translation, as the dynamic terminal always did on that shape, where 3.3.0 returned every element whole; a list read from a subquery, a list in memory and an array are built element by element, and a list selected whole is returned as before.

Security fix and behaviour change (fail-closed): a path beneath a member holding an application's own struct, or a collection of them, takes that member's policy, as a path beneath a framework type has since 3.3.0. A struct is a value, not a navigation: with [DwDenied] on an Iban struct, Iban.Number could be filtered on, and so tested for a guessed value, sorted by, grouped by and returned by a dynamic projection; the typed projection returned it empty only because it skipped structs. The struct member's denials, operators, cost and audit decide every path beneath it, beside the path's own attributes; its alias, required filter, forced scope and description do not. A struct member that is transformed refuses Select, Group and Aggregate on its parts, since its chain has no member of theirs to apply to, while a part that declares its own transform is transformed as any member is. A class is still a navigation whose members are separate fields: a denial of Customer denies only that path.

New: DwCaps.Purposes gives a declared purpose page caps of its own. MaxPageSize and DefaultPageSize bound what one response carries, and a deployment sets them for its screens; an export, a report or a feed reads the same rows under the same field policy and was held to the same page, so it stopped at the first one or walked the rest a page at a time, one statement and one count per page and no single snapshot of the data. A purpose is any name, and a deployment may declare as many as it has: Caps:Purposes:excel:MaxPageSize = 10000 in configuration, or options.Caps.Purposes["excel"] = new DwPageCaps { MaxPageSize = 10_000, DefaultPageSize = 10_000 } in code, and several names may share one DwPageCaps. A query runs under a purpose's caps when its DwPolicyContext.Purpose names it, matched as a purpose-bound rule matches, trimmed and without regard to letter case; a purpose no entry names, or none, runs under the deployment's caps, so a read that forgets to declare itself is bounded like a screen's. A value a purpose leaves null takes the deployment's cap, a value it sets is at least one so no purpose can make a read unbounded, and the default page stays bounded by the maximum. Only the two page caps are replaced; every other cap applies to every purpose alike, and a page past a purpose's maximum is refused, never trimmed, as every cap is. The purpose is the host's statement and never the caller's: a request that could name its own purpose could name its own caps. Purposes bind from configuration with ErrorOnUnknownConfiguration, freeze with the posture, and are compared by the caps that apply when DwPolicy.Configure is called again. Bind now reports a value a property refuses, a cap below one or a salt too short, as the InvalidOperationException it documents, with the property's own refusal inside; it arrived as a TargetInvocationException.

Behaviour change: DwPolicyContext.Purpose is stored trimmed, and a blank value is none. A rule's purpose was already trimmed where the rule is built, so a context declaring " export " now means to a purpose-bound rule what it means to a purpose's caps.

Behaviour change: under the strict tier, a filter, order, grouping key, aggregated field, having or segment condition naming a path through a member a projection builds by calling an application type's constructor with arguments is refused as an unknown name is, where EF Core used to throw. EF Core follows a member only through an initializer's binding: new LocalizedText(t.NameAr, t.NameEn).Ar cannot be translated, and new LocalizedText { Ar = t.NameAr, En = t.NameEn }.Ar is t.NameAr. A row built by its own constructor, a positional record, has every member a clause names refused, and a clause on the constructed member itself, ORDER BY Name, is refused too; a member an initializer binds beside the constructor stays usable, and a conditional that builds the member with a constructor in either branch refuses what that branch leaves unbound. Left alone: an anonymous type, whose constructor names its members; the framework's own types, which a provider may translate; a type the model stores as a column somewhere, such as a spatial point; a projection with no entity behind it; and the convenience tier and a dry run, which still fail as an unguarded query does. A selection through such a member still works, because EF Core evaluates the last projection on the client.

Fix: a typed selection naming a path beneath a struct returned the struct's default with nothing refused: Select(["Name.Ar"]) over a LocalizedText struct gave an empty name, guarded or not. The typed projection now builds an application's own struct member by member, as it builds a class navigation, so the row carries what was named and nothing beside it; a nullable one is named through Value, Alias.Value.Ar, and built where it has a value. A path beneath a framework type, Born.Year or Code.Length, still leaves the member unbound, because a typed row cannot hold the year apart from the date and the date whole would be more than the path names; the dynamic terminal carries such a path as it names it. A struct member that is itself a class navigation, a read-only member, the whole of a nullable struct's Value and its HasValue alone are left unbound as before. A projection the policy synthesizes, for a request with no Selects, narrows a struct holding a denied member as it narrows a class, where it used to leave the struct out whole with its allowed members empty; a nullable struct, or one in a collection that is not a list or an array, is still left out whole. And a guarded selection through a struct carries only what was named: the gate added the Id of every node a selected path passes through, as the builder adds a class's key, and read a struct as one, so DeniedBy.Value.Why came back with the struct's Id beside it, typed and dynamic, and a struct whose Id is denied had a selection of its other members refused and was left out of a synthesized projection. Neither builder adds a struct's key, so neither does the gate.

v3.3.0 — A second host may configure the same posture, a path no database can compute is refused rather than run, a path or a member the attribute walk cannot name is still policed, a malformed request is refused as one rather than reaching the caller as a server error, a token vault can hold a key, and Clone is public on the three request types.

v3.2.0 — A row projected before ApplyPolicy keeps its nested objects and lists, denials the policy gate could not see are enforced, a declared default order reaches projected rows, and every asynchronous terminal takes a CancellationToken.

v3.1.0 — Date comparisons that work on every date member, segments combined in the database, five new caps, a stable code where a sentence used to be, preparation enforced whether or not a store is configured, a policy bypass through members named Root, It or Parent closed, a long In list that ended the process fixed, the names the expression parser keeps refused by name, a strict tier that no longer discloses its trace or which fields exist, forced predicates that can let rows with no value through, a declared default order for guarded queries, and refused queries written to the audit.

v3.0.0 — Field-level policies. A new layer that decides what each caller may filter, sort, select, group, aggregate, and see. Additive: nothing enforces until you opt in, and a project with no policy attributes and no DwPolicy.Configure call behaves exactly as 2.1.5.

v2.1.5 — Documentation only. Fixes the XML documentation shipped with the package, which drives IntelliSense in consuming projects: an unescaped generic argument in the Select<T> comment truncated its remarks and returns text, three ToList/ToListAsync overloads were missing the getQueryString parameter description, and CacheReporting.GetQuickHealthSummary documented a parameter it does not take. The library now builds with zero warnings. No API or behaviour changes from 2.1.4.

v2.1.4 — Security and correctness fix. Recommended for all users.

v2.1.3 — Licensing: now published under the MIT license (SPDX: MIT). Free forever for commercial and personal use, with no license acceptance required. No API or behaviour changes from 2.1.2.

v2.1.2 — Fix: ordering by a field path that crosses a collection navigation (e.g. "Tags.Value" on List<Tag>) threw "No property or field 'Value' exists in type 'List`1'". Collection segments are now aggregated to a single comparable value — Min ascending, Max descending — at any nesting depth, translated to SQL and safe over empty collections in memory.
